title: Upgraded by Accident
script: Maya: [surprised] Apparently there's been a mix-up and only one of us has been upgraded, which is going to make the next nine hours slightly uncomfortable.
Idris: [amused] Uncomfortable for you, you mean. I intend to enjoy every reclined inch of business class with a perfectly clear conscience.
Maya: [dry] Naturally. Nothing sharpens someone's conscience quite like the seat already belonging to them.
Idris: [reasonable] To be fair, I didn't request this. The gate agent simply handed me a new boarding pass and wished me a pleasant flight.
Maya: [teasing] And you didn't think to mention that your travelling companion was still stuck back in row forty-two?
Idris: [sheepish] I considered it, briefly, somewhere between the words pleasant and flight.
Maya: [laughing] So chivalry survived roughly four seconds before self-interest quietly took over.
Idris: [wry] I prefer to think of it as pragmatism. Someone has to accept the upgrade, and refusing it wouldn't have moved you forward a single row.
Maya: [conceding] That's an infuriatingly reasonable point, which is exactly the sort of thing that makes it hard to stay annoyed at you.
Idris: [gently] I did ask whether they could move you too. Apparently the flight's fully booked back there, so this was the only seat available.
Maya: [softening] Alright, that redeems you slightly. Though I expect a full report on the champagne, purely for research purposes.
Idris: [smiling] I'll smuggle you a warm towel at the very least, assuming they let economy passengers receive contraband.
Maya: [amused] Nine hours of you describing legroom while I negotiate elbow space with a total stranger. Wonderful.
Idris: [thoughtful] For what it's worth, I'll feel slightly ridiculous the entire flight, knowing you're two curtains away in considerably less comfort.
Maya: [wry] Good. Guilt is the least you owe me, since apparently the champagne is entirely off the table.
Idris: [warmly] Next trip, the upgrade is yours if it happens, no argument whatsoever. I'll even practice looking appropriately guilty in coach.
Maya: [laughing] I'll hold you to that, generously and in writing. Enjoy your curtain of privilege, Idris.
Idris: [grinning] I intend to, quite shamelessly, for at least the first hour.

quiz.question: What has happened with the seating arrangement?
options: Both were upgraded
Only Idris has been upgraded to business class
Both lost their seats
Maya was upgraded instead
quiz.explanation: The gate agent mistakenly upgraded only Idris, leaving Maya in economy.

quiz.question: How does Idris justify accepting the upgrade?
options: He fought hard to get it
He didn't request it, and refusing it wouldn't have moved Maya forward a row
He paid extra for it
He didn't know about the mix-up
quiz.explanation: Idris argues that accepting the upgrade was pragmatic since declining it wouldn't have helped Maya.

quiz.question: Why couldn't Maya also be moved to business class?
options: She refused to pay
The economy section is fully booked, so her seat was the only one available
She didn't want to sit with Idris
The airline ran out of boarding passes
quiz.explanation: Idris explains he asked, but the flight was fully booked, meaning her seat was fixed.

quiz.question: What does Maya ask Idris to do during the flight?
options: Switch seats with her secretly
Give a full report on the champagne, purely for research purposes
Complain to the airline on her behalf
Sleep the entire flight
quiz.explanation: Maya jokingly asks for a full report on the champagne for research purposes.

quiz.question: What does Idris promise for their next trip?
options: He will never fly with Maya again
The upgrade is hers if it happens, without argument
He will buy her a business class ticket
He will always choose economy
quiz.explanation: Idris promises that on the next trip, any upgrade will go to Maya without argument.
